headline: E-money transactions hit 6.4 billion in 2025; PIDM does not directly insure the balances
context: BNM data show e-money transactions rose 27% to 6.4 billion in 2025. PIDM says e-money is not directly protected. Online fraud losses hit a three-year high of RM2.77B, and e-money disputes at the ombudsman, FMOS, more than doubled to 132.

changes.summary: Correction: Replaced a 28 million user figure with BNM's 18.4 billion e-payment transactions in 2025. Added FMOS data (22% of 1,843 e-wallet complaints resolved for the consumer) and removed unverified regional and age figures.

Correction: The headline counted all 18.4 billion e-payments as e-wallet transactions (BNM records 6.4 billion e-money transactions in 2025), ombudsman figures we could not find (1,843 e-wallet complaints, 22% resolved for consumers, 89 days) are replaced by FMOS's published count of 132 e-money disputes, and PIDM's cover is now stated as PIDM gives it: e-money is not directly protected.

Correction: we removed claims we could not confirm against a source (the share of e-wallets holding under RM50, an exclusion in the Consumer Credit Act 2025, scam targeting of women, and party motives behind e-wallet subsidies), and now state the eMADANI programme's terms as the Finance Ministry gave them.

cards.big: E-money users made 6.4 billion transactions in 2025. If an e-wallet issuer fails, PIDM deposit insurance does not cover their balances.
cards.sub: RM2 billion in subsidies onboarded millions since 2020. Online fraud losses hit RM2.77B in 2025, a three-year high.

cards.big: PIDM covers bank deposits up to RM250,000. It calls e-money 'not directly protected': cover reaches e-wallet funds only if the bank holding the trust account fails.
cards.sub: BNM requires non-bank issuers holding RM1 million or more in e-money to keep customers' funds in a trust account at a bank, PIDM says.

cards.big: The financial ombudsman, FMOS, logged 132 e-money disputes in 2025, up from 64 in 2024, mainly over unauthorised transactions from scams.
cards.sub: Across banking and payments, its ombudsman upheld the provider in 887 adjudicated cases in 2025 and ruled for complainants in 334.

cards.big: The RM1B eMADANI e-wallet credit was open to STR recipients and adults earning RM100,000 or less.
cards.sub: MOF said in November 2023 the RM100 credit would reach up to 10 million adults in the B40 and M40 groups.

cards.big: Governments since 2020 paid people to adopt e-wallets. Deposit insurance still does not directly cover the balances.
Like issuing driving licences to millions before building guardrails, then counting the pile-ups as bad luck.
cards.sub: Bank deposits carry PIDM cover up to RM250,000. E-wallet money sits in an issuer's trust account, which PIDM covers only if the bank holding it fails.

cards.big: Three fixes close the gap: tiered deposit protection, capital requirements scaling with operator float, and mandatory literacy in subsidies.
